visuals.heading: How Service Allocation Actually Works

items.text: Clearing the Civil Services Examination gets you onto a merit list.
Service and cadre are two separate decisions, and both matter.

blocks.heading: Avoid When You Fill Your DAF

items.text: IAS field postings, IPS law-and-order duty, and IFS embassy life are very different jobs day to day.
A home cadre is not automatically the right call, and a different-state cadre is not automatically a downgrade.

Allocation is by rank against your submitted preference order, but reserved-category vacancies, prior-cycle carryovers, and how higher-ranked candidates ordered their own preferences all shift the exact cutoff every year.

blocks.heading: Deputation, Global Bodies, and Later-Career Moves

figures.label: Estimated Time Required
figures.source: Officers can be deputed to bodies like the World Bank, International Monetary Fund, Asian Development Bank, or United Nations agencies, usually after around 9 years of service, sometimes earlier in exceptional cases. Five or more years of UN deputation can carry a lifelong tax-free UN pension on top of Indian service benefits.

blocks.sourceSectionTitle: Deputation, global bodies, and later-career moves
supporting: A civil-services career does not stay fixed to one department for 30 years. Deputation, national assignments, and post-retirement moves reshape most officers' paths well before retirement.
